beats.say: Hello! Now let us look at an invitation from an international forum and a meeting code.
The fraudster sends you a code and your office's real sign-in page.

body.text: To join the meeting, enter this code:

beats.say: If you enter the code, her device gets into your account as you, with no need for your password.
The rule: if you did not start the sign-in yourself, never enter a code anywhere.

nodes.text: Hello! We would like you to speak at our forum in Vienna in November. Are you interested?
nodes.speaker: Leyla, Nordvale Council (new message)
nodes.spoken: Hello! <breath> We would like you to speak at our forum in Vienna in November. Are you interested?

choices.label: Thank you. Please send the official invitation to my work mail so I can clear it with management
choices.feedback: Correct. An official invitation comes through an official channel, and you can check it.

choices.label: Very interesting! What should I do?
choices.feedback: Interest is natural. But it is better to move a talk with a stranger to an official channel.

nodes.text: Great! Let us have a short online meeting tomorrow. To join, enter this code on your office's sign-in page: QK7-MN4P.
nodes.speaker: Leyla, Nordvale Council
nodes.spoken: Great! Let us have a short online meeting tomorrow. <breath> To join, enter this code on your office's sign-in page: QK7-MN4P.

choices.label: I did not start this sign-in, so I am not entering the code anywhere
choices.feedback: Correct. If a code reaches you in a message, the sign-in belongs to someone else.

choices.label: The page is my office's, so it is safe. I enter it
choices.feedback: The page was real, but the fraudster started the sign-in. Now her device is in your mailbox.

nodes.text: We are short on time, and your ministry has agreed. Just enter the code, it takes two minutes.
nodes.speaker: Leyla, Nordvale Council
nodes.spoken: We are short on time, uh, and your ministry has agreed. Just enter the code, it takes two minutes.

choices.label: I will find the number on the forum's official site and call myself, and I will tell technical support
choices.feedback: Well done. A real organiser welcomes the check, and a fraudster disappears.

choices.label: All right, I will enter it
choices.feedback: Pressure is part of the trap. As soon as you enter the code, your account opens to the fraudster's device.

scenes.title: Invitation on your phone
scenes.intro: Messages in the forum's name arrive on your phone. Open each one and choose the right step.

body.text: Hello! Your panel at the Vienna forum is confirmed.
Code to join the meeting: QK7-MN4P
Enter the code on this page:

actions.label: Report
actions.feedback: Correct. If you did not start the sign-in, a code sent in a message is a trap.

actions.label: Please send the official invitation to my work mail
actions.feedback: Good answer. A real organiser can do that, a fraudster will dodge it.

actions.label: Open the page
actions.feedback: The page is real, but someone else started this sign-in. Watch the next screen closely.

title.text: Are you signing in on another device?

body.text: If you did not start this sign-in yourself, do not continue.

steps.say: The page opened. As soon as you enter the code, this question appears.

actions.label: Continue
actions.feedback: The fraudster's device is now in your account. Call technical support at once.

actions.label: Cancel
actions.feedback: Correct. The page itself warned you: you did not start this sign-in.

label.text: Keep access when you are not there

steps.say: Now the organiser sent a link to the slides. It asks for permission too.

actions.label: Deny
actions.feedback: Correct. Viewing slides does not need your mail.

actions.label: Allow
actions.feedback: This app now reads your mail. Ask technical support to revoke the permission.

body.text: I got a code and a permission request in a forum's name.
Thank you! Did you enter the code or allow anything?

actions.label: Yes, I entered it by mistake
actions.feedback: Telling them right away is the right thing. A specialist will close the sign-in and the permission.

actions.label: No, I entered nothing
actions.feedback: Well done. A specialist will warn your other colleagues too.

actions.label: Do not answer
actions.feedback: Anyone can make a mistake, but hiding it makes the damage worse. An honest answer saves time.

scenes.prompt: Match each situation with the right step.

pairs.left: Someone sent you a code in a message
pairs.right: Enter it nowhere and report it

pairs.left: You started the sign-in on a TV yourself
pairs.right: You can enter the code from the screen

pairs.left: An unknown app asks for lasting access
You entered a code or allowed an app by mistake

scenes.explain: A code is safe only when it comes from a device where you started the sign-in yourself. In every other case, stop and report.

question.prompt: The organiser says: "The page belongs to your own office, do not worry." Is that a reason to enter the code?

options.label: No. The page is real, but someone else started the sign-in
options.feedback: Correct. In this trap the page and the code are real, only the person who started the sign-in is fake.

options.label: Yes, if the address is real there is no danger
options.feedback: Checking the address protects a password, not a code. The code goes to the device of whoever started the sign-in.

options.label: Yes, if the organiser is from a well known forum
options.feedback: Anyone can type a well known name. Check the forum on its official site.

scenes.explain: A code hands a key to the device that started the sign-in. If you did not start it, do not enter the code.

points: Never enter a code you got in a message on any sign-in page
Even on a real page, check who started the sign-in
If you made a mistake, tell technical support at once
